sections.markdown:
## C — Driving test requirements: vision screening, knowledge test, skills test and medical reporting

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A07
In Maryland you need a driver's license before you drive any motor vehicle, and cars, vans and pick-up trucks all count as motor vehicles. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A07
The licensing requirements are three tests you must pass: a vision screening, a knowledge test and a driving skills test. [A07]
Why it matters: questions often ask which checks stand between an applicant and a license; all three are required.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A07
Some applicants must meet extra requirements to show they can drive safely, and the MVA tells you if that applies to you. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A07
The vision screening measures how well you see, and either the MVA or your own eye doctor may perform it. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A07
To qualify for a license you must have binocular vision, meaning both eyes working together. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A07
The minimum visual acuity for a license is 20/40 in each eye. [A07]
Why it matters: the standard applies to each eye separately, not just to both eyes together.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A07
You also need a continuous field of vision of at least 140 degrees. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A07
If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the vision standard, you must wear them every time you drive, and your license will show that restriction. [A07]
Why it matters: driving without the required lenses breaks a condition printed on your own license.
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A07
Applicants who do not meet the vision standards can find more information on the MVA website. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A07
The knowledge test checks what you know about three areas: motor vehicle laws, safe driving practices and traffic signs. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A07
Everything the knowledge test covers is in the driver's manual, and you take the test at an MVA location. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A07
If you need special accommodations for the knowledge test, the manual sends you to Section 2.A for how to arrange them. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A07
The MVA website offers an Online Driver Test Tutorial with practice questions, and the manual says to study all of its contents as well. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A07
The driving skills test is how the MVA confirms you can drive safely and responsibly, and it combines driving on public roads with a special course at the test site. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A07
The skills test requires an appointment, which you can book on the MVA website or by phone. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A08
You bring your own vehicle to the skills test, and it must carry current license plates and registration. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A08
You must be able to prove that the vehicle you use for the skills test is insured. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A08
The test vehicle must be safe to drive and must have no windshield cracks or other objects that could block your view. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A08
The test vehicle needs at least a half tank of gas. [A08]
Why it matters: a vehicle that fails any of these conditions cannot be used, so the test cannot go ahead in it.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A08
A supervising driver must accompany you to the test site, and Section 10 of the manual explains who qualifies as one. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A08
During the skills test only you and the examiner may be in the vehicle, except that an MVA-approved interpreter may ride along if you need one. [A08]
Why it matters: the supervising driver brings you to the site but does not ride in the car during the test.
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A08
For health and safety during the test, the MVA encourages fresh air in the car, such as open windows, lets you wear a mask if you choose, and asks you to reschedule if you feel unwell. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A08
State law requires you to tell the MVA about any medical condition that could affect your ability to drive, and Section 10 lists which conditions to report and when. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A08
Littering on Maryland roads can cost up to $1500 or 30 days in prison, and highway crews pick up more than two million pounds of litter from state roads every year. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0008]

Glossary: binocular vision — both eyes working together [A07]. Visual acuity — how sharply you see [A07]. Field of vision — how wide an area you see without moving your eyes [A07]. Supervising driver — the qualified licensed adult who accompanies you to the test [A08].
Memory aid: the three gates to a license are See, Know, Drive — the vision screening, the knowledge test and the skills test [A07].
Misconception: passing the knowledge test does not end testing; the skills test in your own insured, registered vehicle still follows [A08].
